what: When the cursor enters the line-height strip of a centered big-text list (platform·category names), the thumbnail board turns on in .2s, and square thumbnails (9.2vw, gap 1.875% of screen width) pop out on both sides of that row’s text, hugging the text in a line with back.out(1) — each one takes a random .2~.53s, so they pop out staggered. The screen is split into five columns: with the cursor at the far left there are 8 on the left and 4 on the right, and toward the right end it shifts to 4 on the left and 8 on the right, extra items scale down to 0 and hide (.2s), and the rest move into place with .3s back.out(1). Moving to another row crossfades the thumbnails to that row’s image in .2s and they follow down. Cursor indicator (data-fx-part=cursor) it follows the cursor only over the row. On touch screens the row passing the screen center turns on

options.gap: Thumbnail gap (share of screen width), default .01875
